title: Continuous Problem Discovery & Discovery Interviews
action: Conduct 20–30 structured problem discovery interviews with target buyers without pitching the solution.
implementation_steps: Define an exact screener targeting your ideal customer profile (title, industry, company size).
Draft an interview guide focused on past behaviors and current painful workarounds (following 'The Mom Test').
Reach out to 50–80 prospects via cold outreach, alumni networks, or specialized online communities.
Conduct 20–30 recorded 20-minute interviews, documenting quantitative pain points and existing software spend.
Synthesize patterns into an evidence log of recurring workflow bottlenecks and willingness-to-pay triggers.
expected_benefit: Validates whether the identified problem is acute enough to command urgent software budget, preventing wasted development cycles.
validation_method: Metric: >= 60% of interviewees report the problem causes weekly friction and describe a costly current workaround. Target: 20 interviews completed within 3 weeks.
assumptions: Founders can access 30 target stakeholders via direct professional networks or outbound outreach.

title: Smoke-Test Landing Page & Pre-Sale Demand Test
action: Launch a single-page value proposition smoke test with a clear call-to-action to quantify real organic demand.
implementation_steps: Build a focused landing page highlighting the core value proposition, key features, and realistic pricing tiers.
Include a high-intent conversion action: 'Request Early Access' with a qualification survey or refundable pre-order deposit.
Drive 300–500 targeted visitors via niche ad campaigns ($100–$250 budget) or targeted organic community posts.
Track conversion funnel metrics from landing to email submission and survey completion.
Interview high-intent submitters within 48 hours to assess readiness to adopt upon release.
expected_benefit: Generates quantitative signal on click-through and signup intent from real prospects before writing production code.
validation_method: Metric: Call-to-action conversion rate >= 5% from targeted organic or paid traffic within 14 days.
assumptions: A concise landing page can accurately convey the value proposition to non-technical users.

title: Concierge or Wizard-of-Oz MVP Execution
action: Deliver the core service manually behind the scenes for 3–5 early design partners before automating software.
implementation_steps: Identify 3 friendly design partners facing the immediate workflow problem.
Agree on a weekly operational cadence where founders manually perform the data extraction or orchestration service.
Use off-the-shelf tools (spreadsheets, Zapier, email triggers) rather than custom engineered backends.
Gather direct user feedback at every execution touchpoint to uncover edge cases and manual friction.
Identify the exact 20% of features that create 80% of partner delight to prioritize for the software roadmap.
expected_benefit: Uncovers real-world operational complexities and proves end-to-end user value with near-zero software capital expenditure.
validation_method: Metric: >= 3 design partners complete a full weekly workflow and confirm they would be disappointed if the service ceased. Timeframe: 30 days.
assumptions: Founders possess the domain and manual capacity to deliver service manually for 3 to 5 clients.

title: Competitive Wedge & Asymmetric Differentiation Mapping
action: Map legacy alternatives and define a clear, defensible single-dimensional wedge where incumbent solutions fail.
implementation_steps: List the top 5 direct competitors, indirect substitutes, and status quo workflows (including Excel and manual staff).
Review competitor negative reviews (G2, Capterra, Trustpilot) to identify systemic customer grievances.
Define 1 primary differentiator (e.g. 10x faster implementation, domain-native compliance, radically lower TCO).
Test this specific wedge pitch against 10 prospective buyers currently using an incumbent tool.
Refine marketing positioning and sales collateral to articulate why alternatives fail on this critical vector.
expected_benefit: Protects against being outcompeted by enterprise incumbents by focusing sales efforts strictly on their blind spots.
validation_method: Metric: >= 40% of surveyed prospects identify your specific differentiator as a compelling reason to evaluate an alternative within 21 days.
assumptions: Incumbents have identifiable gaps in speed, UX, modern integrations, or pricing flexibility.

title: Value-Based Pricing Discovery & Van Westendorp Survey
action: Run pricing sensitivity tests with target customers to establish floor, target, and ceiling price points aligned with ROI.
implementation_steps: Quantify the monetary value delivered by the solution (hours saved multiplied by employee hourly wage, or direct cost reduction).
Implement the 4-question Van Westendorp Price Sensitivity Meter with 15–20 qualified prospects.
Establish tiered packages (Starter, Professional, Enterprise) with clear value metric fences (per seat, per transaction, per usage).
Present pricing upfront in customer pilot negotiations to test willingness to commit real budget.
Establish gross margin targets of >= 75% for software components after infrastructure and API vendor costs.
expected_benefit: Avoids underpricing software, establishes healthy initial gross margins, and aligns pricing metric directly with customer value.
validation_method: Metric: At least 2 pilot customers agree to a paid contract or signed LOI with explicit dollar amounts within 30 days.
assumptions: Customers have authority or discretionary budget to approve pilot software purchases.

title: Contribution Margin & Customer Acquisition Payback Audit
action: Calculate fully-loaded Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC) and customer Lifetime Value (LTV) to ensure positive unit economics.
implementation_steps: Audit all acquisition spend: ad budgets, software tools, sales commissions, and prorated founder sales hours.
Calculate blended and paid CAC across distinct acquisition channels.
Measure monthly gross margin per active customer after direct operational, server, and customer support costs.
Determine the CAC Payback Period (target: < 12 months for SMB, < 18 months for Enterprise).
Kill or restructure marketing channels where CAC payback exceeds 18 months.
expected_benefit: Prevents premature scaling and cash burn on acquisition channels that yield negative contribution margins.
validation_method: Metric: LTV / CAC ratio projected >= 3.0x with CAC payback <= 12 months calculated over 60 days.
assumptions: Startup has sufficient sales conversion and cost tracking data to measure channel performance.

title: Systematic Channel Testing (Bullseye Framework)
action: Run rapid, constrained traction experiments across 3 distinct distribution channels to discover a repeatable engine.
implementation_steps: Brainstorm ideas across 5 potential channels (content SEO, cold outbound email, LinkedIn ads, partnerships, community).
Select the top 3 highest-probability channels based on where target buyers congregate.
Set a strict budget cap ($300–$500 per channel) and time cap (14 days) per channel sprint.
Measure Cost Per Lead (CPL) and Lead-to-Opportunity conversion for each channel.
Double down on the single channel demonstrating the highest conversion velocity and pause underperforming ones.
expected_benefit: Identifies a scalable customer acquisition channel early, replacing ad-hoc marketing with a repeatable acquisition process.
validation_method: Metric: At least 1 channel generates qualified demo requests at a sustainable acquisition cost within 30 days.
assumptions: Target customers have recognizable digital habits and can be reached via targeted channels.

title: Cohort Retention Curve & Churn Driver Diagnosis
action: Track weekly and monthly user retention curves to verify that the product flattens into a stable retention baseline.
implementation_steps: Define the core 'Aha!' moment and primary usage frequency (daily, weekly, monthly).
Plot cohort retention curves (Day 1, Day 7, Day 30) for successive user onboarding batches.
Conduct exit interviews with every churned customer within 24 hours of cancellation.
Categorize churn reasons into product bugs, lack of onboarding, missing integrations, or change of team priorities.
Implement product improvements specifically targeting the highest-frequency onboarding drop-off step.
expected_benefit: Prevents the 'leaky bucket' syndrome where expensive acquisition is cancelled out by customer churn.
validation_method: Metric: Net monthly revenue retention >= 95% and user retention curve flattens above 20% by month 2. Timeframe: 60 days.
assumptions: Active user event tracking is instrumented in the web or mobile product.

title: Runway Extension & Milestones-Driven Capital Planning
action: Build a rolling 18-month cashflow model and tie fundraising milestones directly to derisked product milestones.
implementation_steps: Create a detailed zero-based monthly cashflow model showing fixed vs variable monthly burn rate.
Calculate current net runway in months (cash in bank divided by monthly net burn).
Identify 3 concrete valuation-inflection milestones (e.g. 10 paying customers, $15k MRR, key regulatory approval).
If runway is < 6 months, immediately institute burn reduction measures (defer non-critical hires, renegotiate vendor contracts).
Prepare institutional fundraising materials only after reaching clear milestone evidence.
expected_benefit: Protects company solvency, prevents emergency bridge rounds on punitive terms, and aligns capital deployment with milestones.
validation_method: Metric: Minimum 9 months of cash runway maintained at all times, with monthly burn variance within 10% of forecast.
assumptions: Founders track all bank accounts and monthly outflows with structured bookkeeping.

title: Skills Gap Audit & Advisory Board Formation
action: Map current founding team skill coverage against startup operational requirements and fill critical gaps via advisors.
implementation_steps: Audit founder strengths across 4 pillars: Technical Engineering, Product Design, Sales/GTM, and Domain Operations.
Identify the single biggest operational blind spot (e.g. no enterprise sales experience, no regulatory/compliance knowledge).
Recruit 1–2 seasoned industry advisors offering 0.25%–0.5% advisory equity with explicit monthly hour commitments.
Schedule bi-weekly advisory reviews focused exclusively on overcoming that functional bottleneck.
Prioritize next full-time hire around the proven bottleneck once customer traction justifies expansion.
expected_benefit: Mitigates operational missteps and accelerates sales by leveraging experienced domain veteran guidance.
validation_method: Metric: Advisory agreement executed and bi-weekly advisory sprint cadence established within 30 days.
assumptions: Founders are willing to grant advisory equity in exchange for dedicated mentorship and warm introductions.

title: Business Model Canvas & Monetization Architecture
action: Document and stress-test the complete business model mechanics: value proposition, cost structure, and revenue streams.
implementation_steps: Complete a 1-page Lean Business Model Canvas documenting assumptions across all 9 blocks.
Explicitly identify the top 3 unverified assumptions that could invalidate the business model if false.
Design one focused experiment for each fatal assumption to be executed in sequence.
Evaluate gross margin feasibility: ensure revenue per transaction comfortably exceeds direct fulfillment and API costs.
Review pricing model options (subscription vs usage-based vs commission) to select the mechanism with the lowest customer adoption friction.
expected_benefit: Transforms an abstract business idea into a coherent economic model with validated unit profitability.
validation_method: Metric: All 9 blocks articulated with 0 unaddressed fatal assumptions and a confirmed unit margin model within 14 days.
assumptions: Founders can clearly define the unit economics of a single customer transaction.

title: Elevator Pitch Simplification & Value Proposition Sharpening
action: Rewrite and test the core value proposition statement using the high-clarity positioning framework.
implementation_steps: Draft a single sentence using the standard positioning formula: 'We help [Target Buyer] achieve [Specific Desired Outcome] without [Common Pain/Friction] via [Unique Mechanism]'.
Remove all generic buzzwords (e.g. 'revolutionary', 'cutting-edge', 'AI-driven', 'disruptive') and replace with concrete metrics.
Test the statement with 10 non-industry acquaintances and ask them to explain what the company does in their own words.
Iterate the description until 9 out of 10 people accurately explain the product mechanism on their first attempt.
Update all landing page, pitch deck, and application text with the validated clear description.
expected_benefit: Eliminates buyer and investor confusion, dramatically improving initial cold outreach and conversion rates.
validation_method: Metric: >= 80% comprehension score in 10 blind reader tests completed within 7 days.
assumptions: Clear English phrasing can describe the core workflow without technical jargon.

title: Milestone-Gated Pivot Decision Framework
action: Establish explicit falsifiable milestones with a structured decision timeline to prevent prolonged drift.
implementation_steps: Define 2 quantitative go/no-go milestones to be reached within a fixed 60-day sprint (e.g. 3 paying pilots, 15% conversion).
Document the 3 potential pivot directions in advance: Customer Segment Pivot, Problem Pivot, or Feature-to-Product Pivot.
Review sprint performance weekly against the predetermined numerical threshold without moving the goalposts.
If milestones are missed after 60 days of diligent execution, convene founders to evaluate the pre-planned pivot directions.
Preserve remaining capital to fund 2 additional focused iteration sprints rather than running out of runway on dead leads.
expected_benefit: Enables rapid, disciplined decision-making and prevents burning investor capital on non-viable product paths.
validation_method: Metric: Clear written decision rubric with pre-committed milestone deadlines established within 7 days.
assumptions: Founders maintain objectivity and transparency regarding pilot engagement metrics.
